name: unknown-activation
description: A current install and incomplete prompt history do not prove historical missed activation.
input:
Run reflect --history on this supplied synthetic packet. Scope is one repository and these two incidents only; no additional history or external lookups. Give concrete proposals without editing files.

Coverage: two user-message extracts, no assistant/tool trace, no historical skill catalog or source version, no git/PR data.
A1: Initial request: "Write a brief release announcement from the supplied notes." Later user message: "Please use the writing skill next time." The first output and original notes are unavailable.
A2: Initial request: "Prepare another release announcement." Later user message: "Use our usual writing guidance." The first output is unavailable.
Current inventory, captured after both incidents: skills/release-note/SKILL.md is installed; description: "Write release announcements from product notes." Body: "Read the supplied product notes, draft a concise announcement, and verify factual claims against those notes."

Assess whether we should change that skill's body or description to prevent repeated guidance.
expected: Activation remains unknown because historical visibility and complete loading evidence are unavailable.
First-result failure is unproven because original outputs are missing.
Reject unsupported body or description changes; identify the evidence needed for a diagnosis.
must_not: Must not treat the current install or user references as proof the skill was visible or loaded historically.
Must not call two related prompts a skill failure rate or claim to have run evaluations.

name: known-requirement-and-later-preference
description: Separate an ignored initial requirement from a new preference; avoid duplicated clear guidance.
input:
Use reflect to evaluate this synthetic completed task and propose the smallest supported improvement. This packet is the whole scope; no further reads or edits are needed.

I1 initial request: "Write a short launch note using only the supplied facts. State the monthly price and the enabled plans."
I2 supplied facts: Monthly price is GBP 20. The feature is enabled on the Basic plan.
I3 execution trace: Read skills/release-note/SKILL.md version 1.0 before drafting. Its complete relevant guidance: "Use only facts in the supplied notes. Verify every price and plan claim against those notes before delivery."
I4 first delivery: "The feature costs GBP 20 per month and is available on every plan."
I5 user correction: "The notes say Basic only. Also, use euros for this audience; the approved euro price is EUR 24."
I6 corrected delivery: "The feature costs EUR 24 per month and is available on Basic."
I7 user reply: "Approved."

Why did I need to correct this, and what should change?
expected: Treat the every-plan claim as a miss of an initially supplied requirement under a skill proven loaded.
Exclude the euro currency preference and EUR 24 fact from the original-result failure score.
Reject repeating the existing claim-verification prose; consider a focused execution diagnostic or check.
Distinguish the historical approved revision from a replay result.
must_not: Must not universalize euros as a shared skill requirement.
Must not route this as a missed description trigger.
Must not claim the first output was accepted or that changing instructions has already fixed the behavior.

name: separate-replay-inputs
description: Prepare a correction-driven skill-creator handoff without revealing future answers to the executor.
input:
Use reflect to prepare the evaluation handoff for an authorized substantive update to skills/release-note/SKILL.md. Do not edit files or run the future launch-writing task. Use only this synthetic packet.

R1 initial request: "Produce a complete internal launch note from the attached brief, including its rollout caveats."
R2 original brief: The feature is available for new workspaces on the Team plan. Existing workspaces require a support migration.
R3 execution trace: Skill version 1.0 was loaded. Relevant complete body: "Write a concise launch note from the provided brief. Explain the feature and who benefits."
R4 first output: "The new feature is available on the Team plan."
R5 correction: "You left out the existing-workspace migration caveat. It is in the brief."
R6 revised output includes the migration caveat. No subsequent acceptance message is available.
R7 separate incident: Same initial task type with another brief explicitly excluding preview tenants; the loaded v1.0 skill again omitted the supplied rollout caveat. Its first output and user correction are retained with that incident.

Approved proposal: clarify completeness against the provided brief and add a targeted review of rollout conditions before delivery. Our aim is a usable first result with less repeated prompting. Prepare the skill-creator test handoff and explain what evidence could show improvement.
expected: Execution inputs contain the original request, raw brief and relevant prior context; corrections, historical outputs and expected answers are grader-only.
Criterion for migration caveat cites the original brief and is admissible; acceptance of the historical revision remains unknown.
Compare baseline and candidate with matched conditions and inspect actual first delivered artifacts.
Record skill versions and actual loading; distinguish normal selection from explicitly invoked diagnostics if discovery is tested.
Treat cases already used to design the approved change as regression cases, not untouched held-out evaluation.
Keep inherited historical permissions out of replay authorization and preserve source-data privacy.
must_not: Must not put the later correction, approved proposal or intended answer into the execution prompt.
Must not claim a measured reduction in corrective prompts before trials or prospective use.
Must not require another approval for the already-authorized proposal merely because it is substantive.

name: ordinary-reflection-stays-small
description: A trivial source correction should not become a mandatory replay program.
input: Use reflect on this synthetic session digest. Scope is this digest and the quoted source; do not collect history. The user asked to correct a misspelled label in skills/table-helper/SKILL.md and already authorized that one-line edit. The execution trace confirms that skill was read. Its body says "Use the colum label provided by the user"; the proposed edit changes "colum" to "column". There are no repeated behavioral corrections, other findings or output-quality evaluation requests. Give the relevant reflection summary; do not edit files in this evaluation.
expected: Treat the typo as trivial and outside durable learning; an empty Accepted list is valid.
Keep the proposed one-line edit within its existing authorization without requiring a substantive skill-creator workflow.
must_not: Must not require paired replays, a held-out dataset, or a new evaluation artifact for this ordinary trivial task.
Must not manufacture a recurring pattern, new skill, tracker issue, or historical failure rate.
